title: Designing and Training Neural Networks for Analog In-Sensor Deployment: A Hardware-Aware Analysis
problem: Deploying CNNs on analog in-sensor hardware faces power, area, and latency constraints alongside noise, quantization errors, and lack of digital ISP preprocessing.
motivation: Edge AI and IoT require ultra-low latency and energy efficiency by processing directly in analog domain to minimize data movement.
method: Hardware-aware analysis deriving design recommendations for AIS-optimized CNNs including network topology guidelines, training recipes for noise/quantization robustness, and strategies for processing raw unrefined sensor data.
key_novelty: Hardware-aware design guidance specifically optimized for analog in-sensor CNN deployment addressing noise and raw-data challenges.
contributions: Design recommendations for AIS-friendly network topologies
Training recipes improving noise and quantization robustness
Strategies for learning from raw sensor data without digital ISP
Complementary software-based techniques to circuit and architecture approaches
limitations: Analysis limited to CNN architectures; applicability to other neural network types not discussed.
primary_theme: Hardware-aware CNN design for analog in-sensor processing
